title: E-GRV-0136: a forming headroom horizon has no late part and no thermal part, and slower growth strips the quench...
purpose: Experiment E-GRV-0136 in the gravity arena: a forming headroom horizon has no late part and no thermal part, and slower growth strips the quench, fail on K3 (the early split's error bound): at C 25, out packets at 4 .. 13 T read 48 / kappa after the lump settles give |beta / alpha|^2 1.9e-8 .. 1.8e-7 of the prompt value at $t_g$ x 1 and x 16 (derived: about 1e-4, from the packet's envelope; a Hawking part would give 1), because the capped redshift makes the settled lump a static reflecting wall; growing 4 and 16 times slower drops the prompt 4 T value 3.63e-2, 3.05e-3, 1.89e-3 (slopes on $\ln t_g$ -1.06 .. -0.80, the 13 T one on the gate's edge), tracking the dock changes the packet meets (3016, 1267, 783), and the spectrum flattens (power law -1.46, -0.89, -0.87; Planck fits at the 30 T edge), away from Planck, not toward it; the window holds 0.634 of a period at omega_C, so no thermal part can form below C about 160; x 1 reproduces E-GRV-0132 to 2.8e-4, the static lump reads 2.5e-24, the integer rule reverses bit for bit through both schedules; the split's error bound reaches 0.153 (gate 0.05) though R1 shows it about 250 times loose.
known_limitations: Depth L2 (L2: known physics reproduced on a stated model).
